findings.description: Root Dockerfile, stage `builder`: at the install step only package*.json and tsconfig.json have been copied (lines 17-18) before `RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps` (line 20). The repository's `scripts/` directory (which the package.json postinstall hook executes) only arrives with `COPY . .` at line 26, after the install. npm ci therefore runs the postinstall hook in a tree where scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs does not exist and the RUN step exits 1.

postinstall runs node scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs && node scripts/copy-cesium-assets.cjs
scripts/ is not excluded, so the ordering (not the ignore file) is why it is absent at line 20

findings.description: Root Dockerfile, stage `production-base`: `COPY package*.json ./` (line 35) then `RUN npm ci --omit=dev --legacy-peer-deps` (line 37) again without --ignore-scripts, so the same postinstall hook runs with no scripts/ present. This stage never receives scripts/ at all: the later COPY --from=builder lines (41-50) copy node_modules/.prisma, @prisma/client, dist, server, src, app, config, types, stubs and root *.ts only. Additionally, with --omit=dev the `prisma` CLI (a devDependency, package.json:169) is not installed, so even if the hook script existed its `npx prisma generate` would have to fetch prisma at build time.

findings.description: package.json declares exactly one npm lifecycle script that fires on install: `postinstall` (no preinstall/install/prepare). It chains two node scripts. scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs sets a dummy DATABASE_URL and spawns `npx prisma generate` (exits with the child status); scripts/copy-cesium-assets.cjs copies node_modules/cesium/Build/Cesium/{Assets,Widgets,Workers,ThirdParty} into public/cesium and exits 1 if the cesium build dir is missing. Both are resolved relative to the install cwd (`node scripts/...`), so their absence makes the hook, and therefore npm ci, fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before either body runs.

evidence.note: dummy DATABASE_URL fallback, spawnSync npx prisma generate, exit with child status
source path under node_modules/cesium; hard exit 1 when missing
copies four Cesium subdirectories into public/cesium
cesium is a runtime dependency
@prisma/client is a runtime dependency

findings.description: docker-compose.staging.yml is the declared full-stack staging build and points at the defective root Dockerfile: `build: { context: ., dockerfile: Dockerfile, target: web }`. Target `web` derives from production-base (line 58), which derives from builder via COPY --from, so a staging compose build executes both defective install steps (line 20 first). cloudbuild.yaml likewise builds all four service images (web, gdpr-worker, search-indexer-worker, domstol-rss-worker) from `-f Dockerfile` with `--target` set to those stage names; every one of these targets sits on production-base.

findings.description: Dockerfile.gcp already contains the mitigation for this exact ordering: both of its install steps pass `--ignore-scripts` (builder line 26, production line 51), copy prisma/ and prisma.config.ts before installing, set a dummy DATABASE_URL, and then run `npx prisma generate` explicitly (lines 28 and 53) instead of relying on the postinstall hook. Its production stage also asserts node_modules/.bin/tsx exists (line 52) and copies scripts/ afterwards (line 63). Dockerfile.gcp does NOT replicate the second half of the hook (copy-cesium-assets.cjs), so public/cesium is not populated in that image by the build itself.

evidence.note: builder: prisma inputs copied first, npm ci --ignore-scripts, explicit prisma generate
production: same pattern with --omit=dev, --ignore-scripts, tsx assertion, explicit prisma generate
scripts/ copied only after install

findings.description: .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml is the optional Vercel staging path. It does not build any Docker image: it runs `npm ci` on a full checkout (where scripts/ exists, so the postinstall succeeds), `npm run build`, `prisma migrate deploy`, then the Vercel CLI. Its header explicitly defers full-stack staging (WebSocket, workers, PostGIS) to GCP or docker-compose.staging.yml, i.e. to the defective Dockerfile build contract.
